### Feature summary

**Create Support Ticket** — agents can log tickets with **title**, **description**, **priority**, **status**, and **assignee**, with server-side validation and clear field errors. Scope is **create only** (list/view/update/search are explicitly out of scope).

### Defaults (documented in Assumptions)

- **Priority**: `LOW` | `MEDIUM` | `HIGH` | `URGENT` (default `MEDIUM` if omitted)
- **Status on create**: `OPEN` or `IN_PROGRESS` only (default `OPEN` if omitted)
- **Assignee**: optional (unassigned allowed)
- **Title** required; **description** may be empty

TicketService - the big one with list, search, filter, sort validation, create, update, get

CommentService is next. I'm deciding whether to use TicketSpecifications or inline validation in the service.

Allowed sort fields are createdAt, priority, status, and updatedAt. Priority sorting requires custom logic in the service layer since JPA cannot handle it directly. The list method will validate the pageable, build a Specification, and detect priority sort to apply custom ordering.

Native SQL CASE statements for priority ordering are too limited. Criteria API is the better approach for custom priority sorting.

Several priority sort approaches were rejected. Alphabetical enum ordering is wrong. In-memory sorting breaks pagination. Native query fragments are too complex. Hibernate @Formula is skipped. The repository add method is next.

A default repository method with EntityManager is being considered for priority sorting. Transient formula fields were rejected. Lexicographic string sorting on the priority enum will be used instead. A test will verify that URGENT sorts before LOW.

Lexicographic enum ordering is acceptable for v1. A custom repository interface with EntityManager will handle priority sorting instead of CriteriaBuilder CASE expressions.

Native query with limit and offset was rejected as too messy alongside specifications. Adding a priorityOrder column to the database was also avoided. The controller will validate the page size directly rather than relying on WebConfig.

Page size will be validated in the controller with a BadRequestException for values outside the 1–100 range. Sort fields will be checked against an allowlist before reaching the service. Create validation will require a trimmed, non-blank title.

Create validation will restrict status to OPEN or IN_PROGRESS and default priority to MEDIUM. Updates will accept partial fields, but any provided title must be non-blank. A comment service is being added. The controller will log list failures with SLF4J. OpenApiConfig will be a simple bean. Web
</details></think>

### What was built (backend)

Single Spring Boot app implementing specs **001, 002–010, 012** in one slice:

| Capability | Endpoint |
|------------|----------|
| Create | `POST /api/v1/tickets` |
| List (page/sort) | `GET /api/v1/tickets` |
| View + comments | `GET /api/v1/tickets/{id}` |
| Update (patch) | `PATCH /api/v1/tickets/{id}` |
| Add comment | `POST /api/v1/tickets/{id}/comments` |
| Search | `GET /api/v1/tickets?q=` |
| Filter | `GET /api/v1/tickets?status=` (repeatable) |

## Layered structure applied

Code is reorganized into **api → application → domain ← infrastructure**, matching the updated constitution.

### Package layout (current)

```text
org.ticketflow.be
├── api/              controller, dto, mapper, error, exception
├── application/      service (use cases)
├── domain/           model (entities/enums), exception
└── infrastructure/   config, persistence/repository
```

Tests live under `src/test/java/org/ticketflow/be/api/` and `support/`.

### Constitution **v1.1.0**

Updated [`.specify/memory/constitution.md`](.specify/memory/constitution.md):

- **Principle IV** — layer table, dependency rules (`api` → `application` → `domain`; no controller → repository).
- **Backend Package Layout** — canonical tree for production and test code.
- **Version**: `1.0.0` → **`1.1.0`** (MINOR — expanded architecture guidance).

### Docs synced

- [`specs/002-list-tickets/plan.md`](specs/002-list-tickets/plan.md) — source tree updated.
- All `specs/*/tasks.md` — file paths updated to the new packages (e.g. `infrastructure/config`, `api/controller`).

### Fixes while moving

- `GlobalExceptionHandler` — resolved `FieldError` clash with Spring’s validation type.
- `TicketController` — imports for `TicketMapper` and `BadRequestException`.

Run `./mvnw test` on **JDK 21** to confirm compile after the move.

```text
refactor: align Spring Boot code with api/application/domain/infrastructure layout; constitution v1.1.0
```

python3 <<'PY'
import re
from pathlib import Path

root = Path("/Users/anubhavkhatri/WebstormProjects/TicketFlow/TicketFlowBe/src")

# map old package prefixes to new
subs = [
    ("org.ticketflow.be.api.controller", "org.ticketflow.be.controller"),
    ("org.ticketflow.be.application.service", "org.ticketflow.be.service"),
    ("org.ticketflow.be.infrastructure.persistence.repository", "org.ticketflow.be.repository"),
    ("org.ticketflow.be.infrastructure.config", "org.ticketflow.be.config"),
    ("org.ticketflow.be.api.dto", "org.ticketflow.be.dto"),
    ("org.ticketflow.be.api.mapper", "org.ticketflow.be.mapper"),
    ("org.ticketflow.be.api.error", "org.ticketflow.be.exception"),
    ("org.ticketflow.be.api.exception", "org.ticketflow.be.exception"),
    ("org.ticketflow.be.domain.model", "org.ticketflow.be.domain"),
    ("org.ticketflow.be.domain.exception", "org.ticketflow.be.domain"),
]

pkg_by_dir = {
    "controller": "org.ticketflow.be.controller",
    "service": "org.ticketflow.be.service",
    "repository": "org.ticketflow.be.repository",
    "config": "org.ticketflow.be.config",
    "domain": "org.ticketflow.be.domain",
    "dto": "org.ticketflow.be.dto",
    "exception": "org.ticketflow.be.exception",
    "mapper": "org.ticketflow.be.mapper",
}

for path in root.rglob("*.java"):
    text = path.read_text()
    for old, new in subs:
        text = text.replace(f"package {old}", f"package {new}")
        text = text.replace(f"import {old}", f"import {new}")
    # set package from parent dir under be/
    parts = path.parts
    if "org/ticketflow/be" in str(path):
        for folder, pkg in pkg_by_dir.items():
            if f"/be/{folder}/" in path.as_posix():
                text = re.sub(r"^package\s+[\w.]+;", f"package {pkg};", text, count=1, flags=re.M)
                break
        if path.name.endswith("IT.java") and "/api/" in path.as_posix():
            text = re.sub(r"^package\s+[\w.]+;", "package org.ticketflow.be.controller;", text, count=1, flags=re.M)
    path.write_text(text)

# move test api to controller
troot = root / "test/java/org/ticketflow/be"
api = troot / "api"
ctrl = troot / "controller"
ctrl.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
if api.exists():
    for f in api.glob("*.java"):
        f.rename(ctrl / f.name)
    api.rmdir()
print("done")

## Validation result

**Before:** Updates accepted any `TicketStatus` with no lifecycle rules.

**Now:** Transitions are enforced on **`PATCH /api/v1/tickets/{id}`** when `status` changes.

### Allowed transitions

| From | To |
|------|-----|
| `OPEN` | `IN_PROGRESS`, `CANCELLED` |
| `IN_PROGRESS` | `RESOLVED`, `CANCELLED` |
| `RESOLVED` | `CLOSED` |
| `CLOSED` | *(terminal)* |
| `CANCELLED` | *(terminal)* |

Rejected examples: `CLOSED → OPEN`, `RESOLVED → OPEN`, `CANCELLED → OPEN`, `OPEN → RESOLVED` (skipping `IN_PROGRESS`), etc.

### Implementation

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `domain/TicketStatus.java` | Added `CANCELLED` |
| `domain/TicketStatusTransitions.java` | Transition map + `validateTransition()` |
| `service/TicketService.java` | Validates before `setStatus` on update |
| `specs/.../openapi.yaml` & `data-model.md` | `CANCELLED` + transition docs |
| `README.md` | Lifecycle section |
| `TicketStatusTransitionsTest.java` | Unit tests |
| `TicketStatusTransitionIT.java` | API integration tests |

Invalid transitions → **400** with `code` `VALIDATION_FAILED` and `fieldErrors[].field` = `status`.

**Create** is unchanged: only `OPEN` or `IN_PROGRESS` on create (not `CANCELLED` / `CLOSED`).

Run `./mvnw test` on JDK 21 to confirm.
